en: In this context, if an obstacle—whether caused by fate or by humans—is anticipated during such acts as drawing the dust mandala, such as an affliction from the armies of nāgas, fire, wind, clouds, carnivorous beings, asuras, or elephants arising from the underworld (pātāla), then one should resolve with firm conviction upon a very solid mandala-hall. This hall should be shaped like a peaked pavilion situated within the center of a yellow ten-spoked wheel rotating clockwise; it is presided over by the ten most terrifying Krodhas standing on spikes, located inside a canopy of arrow-nets, a cage of walls, and a rampart of diamond-like earth, all constructed according to the ritual rules.
At every moment, all obstacles are warded off by means of its adamantine nature and other such qualities.

In this context, when drawing a mandala of colored powders and so forth, it is possible that disturbances caused by obstructing spirits may arise from beneath the earth—such as water gushing out, or fire, wind, clouds, lightning, humans, divine hosts, elephants, and the like; whether these are produced by gods or by humans and others. At such a time, one should, according to the ritual procedure, [visualize] the ground as being of the nature of vajra.

Upon the tips of the spokes situated in the space between the enclosure wall, the curtain, the lattice of arrows, and the canopy, there dwell ten extremely terrifying wrathful deities who have empowered them. Upon this yellow ten-spoked wheel, which rotates clockwise, is a celestial mansion (*vimāna*) located in the center of the hub; within this mandala-palace, it is exceedingly firm.
One should cultivate intense conviction for a single moment; by means of the vajra-nature and so forth, all obstacles will be repelled. Thus it is said.

Furthermore, for one who practices uninterruptedly the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) on emptiness whose sole flavor is vast compassion, even immeasurable obstacles are pacified; thus, this sequence does not apply to him. Also, for one who meditates with great firmness on the maṇḍala-circle as having emptiness as its sole flavor, all obstacles and other defects go to destruction without effort and do not even appear in dreams; thus, this sequence does not apply to him either.

Furthermore, for one who cultivates the samādhi of emptiness that is of one taste with uninterrupted great compassion, even immeasurable obstacles will be thoroughly pacified; therefore, these [other] stages do not apply in that case. Thus concludes the procedure for warding off obstacles.
Thus concludes the ritual for averting obstacles.
